title: Building an Equation from Two Points

scenes.title: Two points — how do you get the whole equation?
body: First find how the line moves.
Then use one point to locate the line.
scenes.narration: If you are given two points and asked for the equation of the line, there are really two jobs. First, find how the line moves. That is the slope. Then use one of the points to figure out exactly where that line sits.

scenes.title: Start with (2, 5) and (6, 13)
scenes.narration: Use the points two comma five and six comma thirteen. From the first point to the second, y increases by eight and x increases by four. Slope is change in y divided by change in x, so the slope is eight over four, which simplifies to two.

scenes.title: Now find the missing intercept
scenes.narration: Now use slope-intercept form, y equals m x plus b. We already know m is two. Pick the point two comma five. Substitute x equals two and y equals five. That gives five equals two times two plus b.

scenes.title: Solve for b
scenes.narration: Simplify two times two to get four. Now five equals four plus b, so b equals one. The slope told us how the line moves, and this point told us the vertical position of the line.

scenes.title: The equation is y = 2x + 1
scenes.narration: So the equation is y equals two x plus one. Always check both original points. When x is two, y is five. When x is six, y is thirteen. Both work, so the equation is correct. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
